indication.text: Natazia is an estrogen/progestin combination oral contraceptive (COC) indicated for use by women to prevent pregnancy; efficacy in women with BMI >30 kg/m2 has not been evaluated.

citations.quote: Natazia is an estrogen/progestin COC indicated for use by women to prevent pregnancy. (1)
The efficacy of Natazia in women with a body mass index (BMI) of >30 kg/m2 has not been evaluated. (1, 8, 8)

target_moa.text: Combination oral contraceptive (estradiol valerate, a prodrug of 17β-estradiol, plus the progestin dienogest) that lowers the risk of pregnancy primarily by suppressing ovulation, with changes in cervical secretion and endometrium as additional mechanisms.

citations.quote: COCs lower the risk of becoming pregnant primarily by suppressing ovulation. Other possible mechanisms may include cervical mucus changes that inhibit sperm penetration and endometrial changes that reduce the likelihood of implantation.
The estrogen in Natazia is estradiol valerate, a synthetic prodrug of 17\beta-estradiol.

modality.text: Small molecule (combination of two steroid hormones: estradiol valerate and the progestin dienogest)

citations.quote: EV/DNG represents a new combination oral contraceptive product in the U.S. in regard to utilizing a) estradiol valerate in an oral form, b) a new progestin called dienogest and c) a 4-phasic active drug regimen.

key_safety.text: Most common treatment-emergent adverse reactions (≥2%): headache including migraines (13.2%), metrorrhagia and irregular menstruation (8.0%), breast pain/discomfort/tenderness (6.6%), nausea or vomiting (6.5%), acne (3.9%) and increased weight (2.8%). Serious adverse reactions reported include deep vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver, uterine leiomyoma, and ruptured ovarian cyst.

citations.quote: **Common Treatment-Emergent Adverse Reactions (\ge 2\%):** headache (including migraines) (13.2%), metrorrhagia and irregular menstruation (8.0%), breast pain, discomfort or tenderness (6.6%), nausea or vomiting (6.5%), acne (3.9%) and increased weight (2.8%).
**Serious Adverse Reactions:** deep vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver, uterine leiomyoma, and ruptured ovarian cyst.

detail.text: WARNING: CIGARETTE SMOKING AND SERIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS — Cigarette smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from COC use; this risk increases with age, particularly in women over 35, so COCs should not be used by women over 35 who smoke.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: CIGARETTE SMOKING AND SERIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS

Cigarette smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from combination oral contraceptive (COC) use. This risk increases with age, particularly in women over 35 years of age, and with the number of cigarettes smoked. For this reason, COCs should not be used by women who are over 35 years of age and smoke. [See *Contraindications* (4).]

vote.text: Not presented to an advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues; DRUP did not believe AC guidance was needed to decide approvability for prevention of pregnancy.

citations.quote: Your application was not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable, the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues, the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of a disease, and outside expertise was not necessary.

This Application was not presented to an Advisory Committee (AC) because DRUP did not believe that AC guidance was needed to make a regulatory decision concerning the approvability of the Application for prevention of pregnancy.

detail.text: NDA 022252/Original 1 was reviewed and approved, effective on the date of the action letter; no prior Complete Response Letter for this application is indicated.

citations.quote: We have completed our review of NDA 022252/Original 1, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to your July 2, 2009 New Drug Application (NDA), received July 6, 2009, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Natazia (estradiol valerate and estradiol valerate/dienogest) Tablets.

requirement.text: PMR 1637-1: A prospective, controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study of new users of Natazia and new users of oral contraceptives containing other progestins, expanding the ongoing European INAS-EV surveillance study to include US women, enrolling at least 50,000 women in the US and Europe followed for at least three years to assess thrombotic risks (DVT, PE, acute MI, cerebrovascular accidents).

citations.quote: 1637-1. A prospective, controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study that follows a series of cohorts consisting of new users of Natazia (estradiol valerate and estradiol valerate/dienogest) tablets and new users of oral contraceptives containing other progestins.
The expanded study should enroll a total of at least 50,000 women in the US and Europe, who will be followed for at least three years.
The main clinical outcomes of interest are deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolus (PE), acute myocardial infarction, and cerebrovascular accidents.

summary.text: Natazia (estradiol valerate/dienogest) was approved under a standard NDA (505(b)) for prevention of pregnancy, supported by two pivotal open-label contraceptive trials demonstrating acceptable Pearl Indexes; the application was not referred to an advisory committee, and a 505(o) postmarketing requirement (expanded INAS-EV cohort safety study of thrombotic risk) was imposed.
